heading: Types of Numbers
html:
• Natural Numbers

    • They start from 1

    • Used for counting purposes

    • All positive integers excluding zero

  • Integer

    • All whole numbers: positive, negative and zero.
    • For eg: 0,±1,±2,±30, \pm 1, \pm 2, \pm 30,±1,±2,±3

  • Prime Numbers

    • A number which has exactly two distinct factors: itself and 1

    • 1 is not a prime number

  • Rational Numbers

    • Any number that can be written as a fraction p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0.

  • Irrational Numbers

    • Numbers that cannot be written as simple fractions.

    • Their decimals are non-terminating and non-recurring, e.g. π\piπ

  • Square Numbers

    • The result of multiplying a number by itself twice

    • For eg, 1,4,9,16,25,36,49,64,81,100

  • Cube Numbers

    • Made from multiplying a number by itself three times. For eg, 1,8,27,64,125

  • Reciprocals

    • The reciprocal of a number is 1 divided by that number

    • For eg, Reciprocal of 4 is ¼

    • Zero has no reciprocal

  • Common Multiples

    • A number that is a multiple of two or more given numbers

    • For eg, Common Multiples of 6 and 8 are 24 and 48, as they appear common in both tables of 6 and 8

  • Common factors

    • A number that divides two or more numbers exactly

    • For eg,

      Factors of 12 : 1, 2 , 3 , 4 , 6 and 12

      Factors of 18 : 1, 2 , 3 , 6 , 9 and 18

      Common factors of 12 and 18: 1, 2, 3 and 6

heading: Prime Factorisation
html:
• Writing a number as a product of its prime factors

  • For eg, 60 = 2² x 3 x 5

  • Methods:

    • Factor Tree Method - break the number down step-by-step into primes

    • Division Method - keep dividing by the smallest prime until you reach 1

heading: Highest Common Factor and Lowest Common Multiple
html:
• HCF: Product of common prime factors

  • LCM: Product of all prime factors in the Venn Diagram

heading: Squares and Square Roots
html:
• Square of a number means multiplying it by itself.

    • n2=n×nn^2 = n \times nn2=n×n

  • Square Root is the number that, when squared, gives the original number

    • 32=93^2 = 932=9, so the square root of 9 is 3

    • (−3)2=9(-3)^2 = 9(−3)2=9, so both +3 and -3 are square roots of 9.

    • n2=n\sqrt{n^2} = nn2​=n

  • Examples:

    • 42=164^2 = 1642=16

    • 25=5\sqrt{25} = 525​=5

    • (−72)=49(-7^2) = 49(−72)=49

    • 169=13\sqrt{169} = 13169​=13

heading: Cube and Cube Roots
html:
• Cube of a number means multiplying it by itself three times:

    • n3=n×n×nn^3 = n \times n \times nn3=n×n×n

  • Cube Root is the number that, when cubed, gives the original number

    • n33=n\sqrt[3]{n^3} = n3n3​=n

  • Examples:

    • 23=82^3 = 823=8

    • 273=3\sqrt[3]{27} = 3327​=3

    • (−3)3=−27(-3)^3 = -27(−3)3=−27

    • −643=−4\sqrt[3]{-64} = -43−64​=−4

heading: Other Powers and Roots
html:
• Numbers can have fractional, negative, or higher powers
  • A power tells you how many times to multiply a number by itself.
    • Example: 24=2×2×2×2=162^4 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 1624=2×2×2×2=16
  • A root is the inverse of a power; it ‘undoes’ the power
    • Example: 164=2\sqrt[4]{16} = 2416​=2, because 24=162^4 = 1624=16
  • The nth root of a number xxx is the value which, when raised to the power of nnn, gives xxx.
    • xn=y\sqrt[n]{x} = ynx​=y, yn=xy^n = xyn=x
  • Fractional Indices represent roots and powers together

    • x12=xx^{\frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{x}x21​=x​

    • x13=x3x^{\frac{1}{3}} = \sqrt[3]{x}x31​=3x​

    • xmn=xmnx^{\frac{m}{n}} = \sqrt[n]{x^m}xnm​=nxm​

heading: Accuracy
html:
• Upper Bound - The largest possible value a measurement could be, given its degree of accuracy.

  • Lower Bound - The smallest possible value a measurement could be, given its degree of accuracy.

  • Worked Example

    Q. Find the upper and lower bound of 450 to the nearest 10

    Half the degree of accuracy = 102\frac{10}{2}210​ = 5

    Add to original value for upper bound = 450 + 5 = 455

    Subtract from original value for lower bound = 450 - 5 = 445

heading: Estimation
html:
Significant Figures

  • Significant figures is how precise a number is

Rules for Significant Figures

  • All non-zero digits count

    • 348 →\rightarrow→ 3 s.f

  • Zeros between digits count

    • 406 →\rightarrow→ 3 s.f

  • Leading zeroes do not count

    • 0.54 →\rightarrow→ 2 s.f

  • Trailing zeros count only if there is a decimal

    • 1500 (no decimal) →\rightarrow→ 2 s.f

    • 12.30 →\rightarrow→ 4 s.f

Examples

  • Round to 1 s.f

    • 3.76 →\rightarrow→ 4

    • 248 →\rightarrow→ 200

  • Round to 2 s.f

    • 3.76 →\rightarrow→ 3.8

    • 248 →\rightarrow→ 250

heading: Set Representations
Fractions
html:
• Used to express a part of a whole. eg, 25\frac{2}{5}52​
  • Numerator: The numerator is how many parts you have
  • Denominator: The denominator is how many parts the whole is divided into
  • Proper Fraction: When the numerator is less than the denominator. For example, 38\frac{3}{8}83​
  • Improper Fraction: When the numerator is greater than the denominator. For example, 53\frac{5}{3}35​
  • Mixed Fractions

    • This is only possible for improper fractions

    • A mixed fraction is a whole number with a proper fraction

    • Conversion of an Improper Fraction to a Mixed Fraction:

      The remainder becomes the numerator of the proper fraction, with the denominator remaining the same.

      94=214\frac{9}{4} = 2 \frac{1}{4}49​=241​

heading: Decimals
html:
• Consists of a whole number part and a fractional part separated by a decimal point

  • Recurring Decimals: A digit repeating infinitely after the decimal point (e.g 7.3‾7.\overline{3}7.3 ,which indicates 7.33333….)

  • Recurring Decimals to Fraction :

    • Let x = recurring decimal

    • Let n = number of recurring digits

    • Multiply the recurring decimal by 10n10^n10n

    • Subtract the original recurring decimal from the product above.

    • Solve for x, expressing your answer in the simplest form

heading: Percentages
html: • Per cent means ‘out of a hundred’, referring to values out of 100

heading: Conversions of Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages
html:
• To convert a Percentage to a Decimal

    • Divide by 100

      45%=45100=0.45\text{45} \% = \frac{\text{45}}{100} = 0.4545%=10045​=0.45

  • To convert a Decimal to a Percentage

    • Multiply by 100

      0.7×100=70%\text{0.7} \times 100 = 70 \%0.7×100=70%

  • To convert a Percentage to a Fraction

    • Write the fraction with a denominator of 100 and simplify

      25%=25100=1425\% = \frac{25}{100} = \frac{1}{4}25%=10025​=41​

  • To convert a Fraction to a Percentage

    • Divide the numerator by the denominator and multiply by 100

      1329=0.4482,0.4482×100=44.82%\frac{13}{29} = 0.4482,\quad 0.4482 \times 100 = 44.82 \%2913​=0.4482,0.4482×100=44.82%

heading: Ordering
html:
• === shows when 2 values are equal
  • ≠ when 2 values are not equal
  • >>> when the value on the left-hand side is strictly greater than the right-hand side
  • <<< when the value on the left-hand side is strictly less than the right-hand side
  • ⩾⩾⩾ when the value on the left-hand side is greater than or equal to the right-hand side
  • ⩽⩽⩽ when the value on the left-hand side is less than or equal to the right-hand side

heading: Indices Rules
html:
• When two powers with the same base are multiplied, the values are added
23×24=23+4=27 2^3 \times 2^4 = 2^{3+4} = 2^7 23×24=23+4=27
  • When two powers with the same base are divided, the values are subtracted:
25÷22=25−2=23 2^5 \div 2^2 = 2^{5-2} = 2^3 25÷22=25−2=23
  • Any number raised to the power of 0 equals 1:
50=1 5^0 = 1 50=1
  • When a power is raised to another power, the values are multiplied:
(32)3=32×3=36 (3^2)^3 = 3^{2 \times 3} = 3^6 (32)3=32×3=36
  • A negative power means the reciprocal of the base raised to the positive power:
4−2=142=116 4^{-2} = \frac{1}{4^2} = \frac{1}{16} 4−2=421​=161​
  • A fractional power indicates a root; the denominator is the root, and the numerator is the power:
823=823=643=4 8^{\frac{2}{3}} = \sqrt[3]{8^2} = \sqrt[3]{64} = 4 832​=382​=364​=4

  • When two numbers that share the same exponent, they’re able to share their operation and be raised to the same power.

    22×32=(2×3)22^2 \times 3^2 = (2 \times 3)^222×32=(2×3)2

    22÷32=(23)22^2 \div 3^2 = \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^222÷32=(32​)2

heading: Standard Form
html: • Used to express large or small numbers in factors of 10

heading: To Express Numbers Greater than 000
html:
• Let us take the example of the number 450,000
  • Count the number of digits after the first digit, in this case, 5
  • Take that as the power of 10
  • Place a decimal point after the first number and remove any non-significant 0's
  • 450,000=4.5×105450,000 = 4.5 \times 10^5450,000=4.5×105

heading: To Express Numbers Less than 000
html:
• Let us take the example of the number 0.00031
  • Count the number of digits before the first significant digit, in this case, 4
  • Take that as the negative power of 10
  • Place a decimal point after the first number and remove any non-significant 0's
  • 0.00031=3.1×10−40.00031 = 3.1 \times 10^{-4}0.00031=3.1×10−4

  • To find a percentage of a quantity, multiply the quantity by the percentage (as a decimal).
15 15% \times 200 = \frac{15}{100} \times 200 = 0.15 \times 200 = 30 15

html:
• This is when a value is increased based on the initial start amount (Principal Amount)
  • You can use this formula to calculate the interest amount (You need to add the principal amount again to find the final amount)

html:

Compound Interest=Principal×(1+Rate100)Time \text{Compound Interest} = \text{Principal} \times \left(1 + \frac{\text{Rate}}{100}\right)^{\text{Time}} Compound Interest=Principal×(1+100Rate​)Time

Time Conversions
html:
• 1 Minute = 60 seconds

  • 1 Hour = 60 minutes

  • 1 Year = 365 days (or 366 in a leap year).

  • 1 Day = 24 Hours

  • 1 Week = 7 Days

  • 1 Month = 30/31 Days

  • If you are asked to convert 3 hours into minutes:

    3 hours×60 minutes=180 minutes.3 \text{ hours} \times 60 \text{ minutes} = 180 \text{ minutes}.3 hours×60 minutes=180 minutes.

  • The 12-hour clock uses "a.m." for morning and "p.m." for afternoon/evening.

  • The 24-hour clock uses a continuous format from 00:00 (midnight) to 23:59.

  • Steps to convert 12-hour to 24-hour format:

    • For a.m., keep the time as is but add leading zeros if needed (e.g., 3:15 a.m.=03:153:15 \text{ a.m.} = 03:153:15 a.m.=03:15)
    • For p.m., add 12 to the hour (e.g., 3:15 p.m.=15:153:15 \text{ p.m.} = 15:153:15 p.m.=15:15)

html:
• If it is 10 a.m. in London (GMT) and New York is 5 hours behind, the time in New York is:
